verdict.rationale: GrowthBook's SDK docs show non-boolean flag values, such as `useFeatureValue("button-color", "blue")` returning a string, and a `getFeatureValue` method alongside `isOn`. Rules can serve forced values, and experiment rules assign users across variations, which supports multivariate serving. However, the pack never explicitly documents number or JSON value types, and the runtime probe only exercised a boolean flag. missing for 10: explicit documentation of number and JSON value types, an end-to-end multivariate (more than two variants) config example, independent or hands-on corroboration of non-boolean values.

support.subject: As a developer, I can serve multivariate flags and dynamic configuration values (strings, numbers, JSON), not just booleans

citations.quote: There are 2 main methods for evaluating features: `isOn` and `getFeatureValue`
Layer multiple rules on one feature to compose behavior — for example, a forced value for beta testers above a gradual rollout to everyone else.
you can add an experiment rule to a feature that will randomly assign the users based on some hashing attribute into one of your experiment variations.
